newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech blue chips edge higher to boost PX50.
newsitem.headline: Czech blue chips edge higher to boost PX50.

text.p: Czech shares closed mostly higher on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) on Tuesday, with gains to major issues boosting the PX50 index 1.4 points, or 0.28 percent, to 492.7.
Komercni Banka led the blue chip charge, rising 26 crowns to 1,955. SPT Telecom closed up 16 crowns at 3,041 while CEZ and Ceska Sporitelna were both unchanged.
On the broader market, conference organiser BVV Brno BVVB.BR, a typically low liquidity Czech share prone to erratic price swings, gained 120 crowns to 2,525.
Total volume was moderate at 901,337 shares on turnover of 1.008 billion crowns. Overall, 115 shares gained, while 86 lost ground and 58 closed unchanged.
Despite the gains, dealers warn that the Czech equities market is still plagued by low volumes as investors wait for a resolution to the current instability in the Czech coalition government.

"As soon as interest rates drop and the crown falls further -- and we expect this within the next two weeks -- the stock market will be attractive," said Eugene Klerk of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett. "But given that recession is on the cards, stock selection will be important."
The Czech central bank has raised rates and choked off market liquidity over the past two weeks to support the crown which came under a spirited attack by a wave of investor short-selling.
The crown, which has lost some 10 percent of its value since the onslaught, is expected to come under fire again once rates are eased.
